CLOEXEC: May close handle at exec; neither all descriptors survive nor all close is inferred
CONSEQUENTIAL_HANDLE: Protected regular writable FD, directory/socket/alias authority cannot be accepted as closed from number/path-only snapshot
EXTRA_FDS: Unknown until exact nominated shell collected; even then future fork/exec ordering/source needed
FIRST_EXEC: prlimit is first requested native target in127, interactive shell already running. Actual shell and callsite unbound. Do not insert a new Python interpreter.

POLICY_SOURCE.ALIAS_POLICY: No writable protected regular, directory, socket or duplicated alias at any allowed FD; number alone is not safety

FD0.MODE: O_RDONLY; fstat device/type must be independently verified

FD1.DIRECTION: write to independently bounded outside collector
FD1.OWNER: qualified outside collector same authorized nonprivileged context

FD2.DESTINATION: same combined capture allocation with parent exit tag charged
FD2.DIRECTION: write to independently bounded outside collector

POLICY_SOURCE.OTHER_FDS: All >=3 closed before requested prlimit exec; internal exec-error pipe must be CLOEXEC and not persist into target
POLICY_SOURCE.RACE_POLICY: Caller owns fixed pipe endpoints through fork/exec, no concurrent close/dup2/reopen mutation; no reliance only on pre-fork enumeration or non-atomic CLOEXEC setting

PROTECTED_IDENTITIES: Exact retained protected-path/mount/source pins in124 and131 authenticated; no new host path access performed
SMALLEST_ENTRY_CONTROL_IF_HANDLE_PRESENT: Authenticate actual shell-specific closure or atomically non-inheritable handle policy before first exec; verify caller ownership/races and standard endpoints. No wrapper implementation in132.
STDIO_RELIABILITY_SEPARATE: Bounded pipes/drain/exit cause independent from protected writable handle security
